intro: Strange sightings, failed leads, Christian readings of evil, shadowy games and Westeros revenants—with two complete dark-fiction stories to read. Most picks are from the last fortnight; the September Archive X preview and December 2025 Stoneheart discussion are older discoveries. The November Brides story is a reprint. Major spoilers and mature themes are marked.

items.title: Pilots spot pill-shaped UFO hovering near their plane over Ohio
items.summary: An October report describes an August encounter with a reflective, apparently stationary object at 43,000 feet. The pilots reportedly contacted air traffic control, but neither radar nor their collision-warning system registered it. The account does not establish an alien origin.
items.why: A Why Files-style puzzle: witness descriptions, an apparent sensor mismatch and a brief encounter that leaves competing explanations to examine.

items.title: Last Season
items.summary: A complete new psychological-horror story from The Dark's November issue. After a breakout television role, an actress retreats from auditions into increasingly uneasy idleness, fandom and uncertainty about the boundary between herself and her character.
items.why: Something to settle down and read: creeping identity horror and an unsettling fictional world, with the ending left for you to discover.

items.title: ‘Defend Us From Evil’: Lessons from the Inklings
items.summary: Henry T. Edmondson III reads Charles Williams, C. S. Lewis and Tolkien for their treatment of spiritual evil, temptation, truth and humility. The essay offers a Christian literary interpretation and discusses plots from their books.
items.why: It joins your fantasy reading and theology interests, with routes into the Inklings beyond Middle-earth—especially Williams's supernatural thrillers and Lewis's account of temptation.
items.source: Word on Fire / Henry T. Edmondson III

items.title: Thief Remastered's new expansion is being made by the legendary Black Parade mod team, and it's out next month
items.summary: A first look at The Tarnished Mirror, four new missions connecting the first two Thief games. The Black Parade team promises larger spaces and a return to the series' horror elements; the article examines the trailer's verticality and unusual interiors.
items.why: Your retro and atmospheric-horror tastes meet in shadowy stealth, undead missions and ambitious fan-made level design becoming an official chapter.

items.title: Major update as expedition reaches Amelia Earhart 'plane wreckage'
items.summary: An expedition investigated the Taraia Object in Nikumaroro's lagoon, a satellite-image anomaly thought to resemble Earhart's aircraft. It identified trees instead. This particular lead has closed, while the wider disappearance remains unresolved.
items.why: Follow a tantalising image through to an on-site investigation and see how a persuasive theory fares against physical evidence—a satisfying companion to the more speculative mysteries.

items.title: Stoker’s ‘Dracula’ and True Deliverance from Evil
items.summary: Matthew Malone traces Dracula's literary and folkloric background, then interprets its crucifixes, sacramentals and counterfeit immortality through Catholic theology. Major novel spoilers: the essay discusses the hunters' confrontation with Dracula and the spiritual meaning of its resolution.
items.why: A bridge between supernatural stories and Christian ideas of salvation: why this particular monster needs more than a medical explanation within the novel.

items.title: A Procession of Brides
items.summary: A complete dark-fantasy story reprinted in The Dark's November issue. Frankenstein's Bride narrates her existence through the memories of the murdered women whose bodies formed hers, expanding into encounters with folkloric brides. Contains graphic body horror and sexual violence themes.
items.why: For your request for fantasy literature itself: an unsettling retelling that lets familiar monsters speak for themselves, full of myth and strange transformation.

items.title: After almost a decade of work, Alien: Isolation mod tools hit 1.0 with support for 'full custom maps, missions, modes, characters, weapons, animations, sounds, models, textures, and more'
items.summary: OpenCAGE reaches version 1.0 after years of development, enabling full custom maps and total conversions for Alien: Isolation. Creator Matt Filer demonstrates the possibilities with a Halo-themed project featuring new enemies, cinematics and a custom interface.
items.why: A reason to revisit one of gaming's most oppressive settings—and watch for entirely new horror experiences built on its foundations. The creative possibilities are the draw here.

items.title: AMC Global Media Drops Trailer For New Docu-series, Archive X: Unexplained Phenomena
items.summary: Older September preview, with an embedded trailer, for the ongoing series hosted by Jeffrey Kripal. It draws on Rice University's paranormal-research archives to explore reported abductions, prophetic dreams and encounters with the dead. These are witness claims and programme interpretations, rather than verified paranormal findings.
items.why: A programme to investigate if you enjoy The Why Files: archival material and extraordinary testimony, with questions about consciousness and spiritual experience crossing into your theology interests.

items.category: A Song of Ice and Fire · audio
items.title: Lady Stoneheart: The Revenant of the Riverlands
items.summary: Older gem from December 2025, with an embedded audio episode. Major spoilers through the published novels: History of Westeros examines Stoneheart's vengeance, the Brotherhood's changed purpose and possible future encounters with Jaime, Brienne and Arya. Predictions about those reunions are fan theories.
items.why: Westeros at its most Gothic: resurrection, corrupted justice and the cost of revenge. It connects your appetite for spooky lore with a major book storyline omitted from television.
